statuses.meaning: One best answer: the identifier leads to one target in the requested database.
Several genes or targets are equal in all the evidence that decides; all of them are the best answer, in ascending order of gene id and target id.

reasons.meaning: The identifier is not an identifier of this graph at any release.
The identifier is an Ensembl id, or a sequence accession, with a version this graph does not hold.

step_reasons.meaning: The gene exists at the target release.
The identifier is attached to this gene at the release it is read at.

criteria.meaning: The gene is the queried gene id's own version at the target release (an id that exists at the target release is its own answer).

0: the target is attached to the gene at the target release; 1: attached to a transcript or translation that belonged to the gene at another release; `null`: no gene has an id in the requested database and the gene itself is the target.

candidate_fields.meaning: The Ensembl gene (`<id>.<version>`) at the target release through which the target was reached.
The id in the final database, as that database wrote it at the target release (the gene itself for `ensembl_gene`).

match_steps.meaning: The identifier as written (for an external identifier: as a database wrote it at the release read).
The identifier when letter case is ignored.

match_prefixes.meaning: In a batch: a name made unique by a single-cell tool (another item of the batch with -1, .1 or _1 appended, itself no exact name at the release it is read at alone); the result is that item's.

Unicode was normalised before matching: invisible and control characters (zero-width characters, byte-order marks, bidirectional marks, soft hyphens) removed, compatibility forms (NFKC: full-width letters and digits) and Unicode dashes read as their plain characters.

reading_reasons.meaning: In an organism whose symbols follow a letter-case convention, a string written otherwise that is not exactly a name is read first as a symbol of the organism without letter case, where that names exactly one gene; this reading came after it.

The string ends in a suffix that single-cell tools append to make names unique (-1, .1, _1); reading it, with its separators taken as one or without letter case, as a synonym of another gene than the string before the suffix names is not taken.

place_relations.meaning: On one assembly the two genes overlap (one sequence region, one strand), or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies overlaps it.

On one assembly the two genes do not overlap: another sequence region, another strand, or apart; or a place carried onto the other's assembly by Ensembl's mapping of the two assemblies shares no base with it; or a copy's reference region (Ensembl's assembly exception) shares no base with the other gene; or, on two assemblies that no published mapping joins, they lie on chromosomes of different names (the mitochondrial genome against a chromosome among them), which no assembly change turns one into the other.

bridge_rules.meaning: Taken: the two genes overlap on one assembly, or Ensembl's mapping of their two assemblies carries one onto the other.
Taken: the places of the two genes cannot be compared (two assemblies, a sequence of one name or a scaffold), and no release gives the id to both: the id left one gene for the other.

errors.title: The request is not in the form the endpoint takes.
errors.meaning: The request does not have the shape the endpoint takes: a missing or malformed parameter, a body that is not UTF-8 JSON of the documented shape (`details` lists each problem, `argument` names the parameter when one is at fault).
errors.retry: Change the request: the same request is answered the same way.

errors.title: The request names a parameter the endpoint does not take, or names one twice.
errors.meaning: A query parameter the endpoint does not take, or one given more than once.
errors.retry: Change the request: the same request is answered the same way.

database_kinds.meaning: One of IDTrack's two Ensembl gene namespaces: `ensembl_gene`, the gene id with its version, and `base_ensembl_gene`, without (`versioned` says which).
An external database whose ids are accessions (NCBI's gene numbers in `EntrezGene`, RefSeq's and UniProt's accessions); where the graph holds its labels apart, `labels` names their database.

allowances.meaning: Searching requests (`rate_per_minute` per minute, `rate_burst` at once).
Every other request of the API (`read_share` times the searches' allowance).

source_modes.meaning: An origin is a release (counted only on the assembly that serves it).

cautions.meaning: The best answer is reached through a bridge: where Ensembl's history gives a gene no successor, the walk left it through an id it carries and entered another gene that carries the same id. That is IDTrack's inference; no record of Ensembl states it.

A bridge on the best answer's path joins two genes that both exist at one release: the gene it enters lived beside the gene it leaves rather than after it. A bridge's gene is a plausible successor at that place, not one that Ensembl's history proves, and here the two genes overlap in time.
